title: Add RBACv2 micro-compiler, KMS consent orchestrator, and immutable audit stamps
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces an RBACv2 micro-compiler for constraint validation, runtime KMS consent orchestration middleware, and immutable audit stamps. Backwards-compatible rollout with staged feature flag. See docs/security/rbac-microcompiler.md for migration notes.
description:
Motivation: We need a compact, verifiable runtime for RBACv2 constraints that can be compiled to a small evaluation graph and checked at high QPS without pulling the full policy graph into request-critical paths. This PR introduces a micro-compiler that emits a minimal decision DAG (JSON) for per-route checks, adds a KMS consent orchestrator middleware to validate KMS region pins and consent tokens before key operations, and attaches immutable audit stamps for non-repudiation.

What this changes: - rbac/microcompiler: new package that parses RBACv2 constraint templates and emits a minimal decision DAG used by the request-time guard. The compiler runs at policy-deploy time and outputs compact artifacts stored in policy-store. - api/middleware/kms_consent_orchestrator.go: middleware that enforces KMS region pinning and verifies consent receipts (signed by operator KMS). Includes fallback logic to consult the residency cache when consent is ambiguous. - audit/enricher/immutable_stamp.go: appends an immutable, canonical audit stamp (hash+sig) to every cross-region KMS usage event. - deployment: helm chart tweak to add an opt-in feature flag redwood.rbac.microcompiler.enabled=false by default and a policy-bucket lifecycle hook. - tests: unit and integration coverage for compiler, orchestrator, and audit stamps.

Compatibility and rollout: The micro-compiler is gated behind the feature flag and a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 100%) controlled by the existing rollout service. When disabled, the system continues to use the legacy PDP policy evaluator. The KMS consent orchestrator is opt-in per-namespace; existing tenants see no change until they opt in.

Testing done: - Unit tests for compiler parser, optimizer, and DAG emitter (rbac/microcompiler/*_test.go). - Integration test that deploys a sample policy artifact, exercises route-level checks under 1000 qps in perf-canary harness. - Fuzz test for malformed consent receipts. - CI: lint, go test (pkg), build images, helm lint.

Security review & compliance: We consulted with security and compliance on the audit stamp format; stamps include a deterministic canonicalization of the audit record and a signing envelope tied to the operator key. Migration doc includes suggested retention settings and an explainability endpoint for inspectors to map micro-compiled checks to source policy templates.

Checklist: - [x] micro-compiler: AST -> DAG emitter implemented - [x] KMS consent orchestration middleware implemented - [x] audit stamp appended and verified in ingestion path - [x] feature flags and helm values added - [x] tests and basic perf validation - [x] documentation: docs/security/rbac-microcompiler.md

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the emitted DAG format conservative (no recursion, bounded node types) to simplify on-host evaluation. Follow-ups: a) add a small policy-diff validator to detect semantic changes that require full redeploy, b) add a dashboard in Console to show which tenants have micro-compiled artifacts active.
